clue.text: 51 ladies' men regularly making contact

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals

indicators.note: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so every second letter is kept

parts.note: the even letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A number of womanisers getting in touch with people on a regular basis.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening number is not a quantity of men but a Roman numeral, and the even letters of the next two words follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: To liaise is to keep in touch and cooperate with another party, which is what making contact describes.

clue.text: Prince is banished, retiring conclusively — hence King can relax

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw or fall back, so the letters run backwards
the two letters spelling 'is' are sent away from the name they sit in

parts.note: Louis is a common name for a French prince or king

indicators.note: conclusively means at the conclusion, so only the final letter of each word counts

parts.note: the last letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A prince is exiled and steps down, leaving the king free to unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: LOUIS loses its IS to leave LOU; the final letters E, G, N of 'hence King can' are then read backwards as NGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To lounge is to recline lazily and take things easy, a synonym for unwinding.

clue.text: Something offering support under a broken leg — its problems are largely symbolic

definitions.note: a description of the answer rather than a synonym

indicators.note: in a down clue, being underneath means coming later in the column

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a thing that is broken is smashed and reassembled out of its proper order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged with the A
a bra is an undergarment that supports

explanation.surface: A splint or brace beneath a fractured leg, followed by a remark about symbolism.
explanation.walkthrough: The support is not medical but a piece of underwear, placed below the rearranged A LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Algebra is the branch of mathematics whose problems are worked with letters and symbols standing for numbers.

clue.text: Writer has turned darker

indicators.note: a thing that is turned gets twisted round into a new shape or order

parts.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An author has become gloomier, or perhaps more tanned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' looks like it wants a synonym such as PEN, but the two words together supply exactly the nine letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarthy means dark in complexion, so its comparative form matches the comparative adjective.

clue.text: That woman taking drugs outside is escorting

indicators.note: one piece sits on the outside of another, wrapping round it

parts.note: using is slang for taking drugs
a pronoun for a female person

explanation.surface: A woman doing drugs out in the street while working as an escort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking drugs' suggests a noun such as USER, but the participle is needed so it can be split open around the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Ushering means guiding or showing someone the way, which is what escorting a person involves.

clue.text: Money to support small band after, initially, Paul Young leaves

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting piece sits underneath, so it comes later
coming after means being placed later in the sequence

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of the name
a ring is a circular band
green and greens are slang for money, from the colour of dollar bills

explanation.surface: Cash to keep a little group going once Paul Young, the 1980s pop singer, has left.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Young is a real singer, but here 'Young leaves' is the definition, cutting the name in half. S and RING are split by P.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring greens are young cabbage plants picked before hearts form, eaten as tender leafy vegetables.

clue.text: Go into hospital department with medical drama

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
ER was an American television series set in an emergency room

explanation.surface: Being admitted to a hospital ward amid scenes worthy of a TV drama.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the long-running US hospital series; ENT is the standard hospital abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter a place is simply to go inside it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: One doesn't believe in field manoeuvres

indicators.note: manoeuvres are moves that shift things around into new positions

parts.note: taken as written, seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A sceptic who doubts the value of military exercises in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' reads as part of the phrase 'believe in', but it belongs to the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An infidel is a person without religious faith, someone who rejects a given creed.

clue.text: All in good time — assuming this writer's in shopping arcade

indicators.note: to assume something is to take it on, so one piece takes in another
being in something means sitting inside its letters

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
taken as written
an era is a period of time
the setter referring to themselves

explanation.surface: Telling someone to wait patiently while the writer is busy at the mall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All in good time' is a stock phrase meaning be patient, which disguises the instruction to place one word inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A galleria is a covered passage or mall lined with shops, from the Italian word for gallery.

clue.text: General making son finally abandon biting of nails

indicators.note: to make someone do something is to force a change, here one letter giving way to others

parts.note: general and usual both mean common or normal
S is the abbreviation for son

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so the last letter of each word is kept

parts.note: the last letters of these two words

explanation.surface: An army general who has his son quit the habit of chewing his fingernails.
explanation.walkthrough: In USUAL the S for son is dropped and NG put in its place. 'Biting of nails' looks like one phrase, but 'of nails' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ungual is a technical adjective meaning relating to a nail, claw or hoof, from Latin unguis.

clue.text: Appreciative of, say, charcoal going on fireplace — less smoke at last

indicators.note: going on means being placed after, added onto the end

parts.note: a grate is the metal frame holding a fire

indicators.note: less means minus, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: charcoal is an example of fuel

indicators.note: at last points to the end, so only the final letter is wanted

parts.note: the final letter, which is removed

explanation.surface: Someone thankful for a smokeless fuel being put on the hearth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Less smoke' sounds like smokeless fuel, but it asks for the last letter of 'smoke' to be dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Grateful for something means thankful or appreciative of it; the 'of' stands in for the preposition 'for'.

clue.text: Flashy item couriers supply

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, it means bendily, so the letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, twelve letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A showy product delivered by a parcel service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a verb meaning deliver, but it is the adverb from supple, the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Meretricious means showily attractive but cheap and lacking real value, close to gaudy or flashy.

clue.text: Agent's gamble on game with small note

indicators.note: in an across clue, sitting on something means coming after it

parts.note: Go is a Japanese board game
a bet is a wager
wee is Scottish for small
N is the abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: A secret agent wagers on a match, leaving a short message.
explanation.walkthrough: Go is the ancient Japanese board game, a crossword favourite for 'game'.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-between acts as an intermediary on behalf of others, which is what an agent does.

clue.text: Line raised for example by director briefly when turning over

indicators.note: turning something over flips it, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example
DIR is the short form of director

explanation.surface: A film director, say, raising a line of dialogue while flipping through the script.
explanation.walkthrough: The two abbreviations are joined first and only then is the whole string read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a long narrow raised strip, such as a crest of hills or a raised line on a surface.

clue.text: Astronomer, 19, 20 working to cover eclipse essentially

indicators.note: letters set working are put into action and moved about into a new order

parts.note: the answer to 19-down
the answer to 20-down

indicators.note: the essence of something is its heart, so the central letter is kept

parts.note: the middle letter of this seven-letter word

explanation.surface: An astronomer and two other clues are put to work on covering a solar eclipse.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers point to the answers of 19 and 20; their thirteen letters are rearranged around the central I.
explanation.definitionFit: Galileo Galilei was the Italian scientist who first turned a telescope on the heavens and championed heliocentrism.

clue.text: Stella maybe determined to follow tail of football hooligan?

indicators.note: following means coming after in the sequence

parts.note: Stella Artois is a brand of Belgian beer

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its end, so only the final letter is wanted

parts.note: the final letter of this word
to be out to do something is to be determined to do it

explanation.surface: A drinker of Stella bent on trailing a football thug.
explanation.walkthrough: Stella looks like a woman's name but is the beer. The question mark signals that the definition is broad: a lager lout is a specific kind of hooligan.
explanation.definitionFit: A lager lout is British slang for a young man who becomes rowdy and violent after heavy beer drinking.

clue.text: Has amphibians adopting relatively recent settlements

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in and make part of the family, so one piece is taken inside another

parts.note: newts are small amphibians
to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: Someone keeps frogs and newts in recently built housing estates.
explanation.walkthrough: New towns were planned British towns built after the Second World War, such as Milton Keynes and Stevenage.
explanation.definitionFit: New towns are planned communities built from scratch in the mid twentieth century, so they are comparatively young places.

clue.text: Humour failing at the start — ignore pun about bird

indicators.note: failing at the start means the opening letter gives out and is lost

parts.note: humour in the sense of mood or temperament

indicators.note: about means around or all over the place, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A joke falls flat at the outset, so skip the wordplay and get to the bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humour' points to mood, as in 'in a good humour', not to jokes. TEMPER loses its T.
explanation.definitionFit: The emperor penguin is the largest species of penguin, a flightless bird of Antarctica.

clue.text: Celebrated using timeshare arrangement constituent secured

indicators.note: a timeshare has two parties sharing one property, so here two pieces share a single T

parts.note: a part is a component or constituent
tied means fastened or secured

explanation.surface: Throwing a party on securing a holiday timeshare deal.
explanation.walkthrough: PART ends with T and TIED starts with it; 'timeshare' tells you the two words overlap on that single T rather than doubling it.
explanation.definitionFit: To have partied is to have celebrated at a social gathering, the past tense matching.

clue.text: Criminal and murderer scratching walls on prison — nothing escapes

indicators.note: in a down clue, sitting on top means coming first
the walls of a word are its outer letters, and scratching them out removes them
nothing is the letter O, and escaping means it gets out and goes

parts.note: a killer is a murderer
gaol is the British spelling of jail

explanation.surface: A killer clawing at the walls of his cell, and nobody gets out.
explanation.walkthrough: KILLER loses K and R to give ILLE; GAOL loses its O to give GAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Illegal and criminal both describe something against the law, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: American cutting record up, specifically number one?

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters read from bottom to top
cutting into something means going inside it

parts.note: a log is a written record
A is the abbreviation for American
IE, id est, means that is, or specifically

explanation.surface: An American smashing a record, being, specifically, the top person.
explanation.walkthrough: The goalkeeper traditionally wears the number 1 shirt; the question mark flags that the definition works by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A goalie is the goalkeeper, the player in football who customarily takes the first squad number.

clue.text: Beat hour to book tours

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go all round it, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: taken as written
HR is the abbreviation for hour
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: The time to reserve a sightseeing trip is coming up fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' is not a link word here; it is the piece that goes round the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a strong regular pulse, a beat of the heart or of music.

clue.text: Located immoral diamonds

parts.note: base means low or morally unworthy
D is the abbreviation for the card suit diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone tracked down some illicit gems.
explanation.walkthrough: Diamonds suggests jewels, but in crosswords it often means the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Being based somewhere means being situated or positioned there, close to located.

clue.text: Voice of Looney Tunes' biggest characters appearing in Daffy cartoon

indicators.note: appearing in something means showing up inside it
daffy means silly or crazy, so the letters go haywire

parts.note: taken as written, seven letters to rearrange

indicators.note: the biggest characters in a title are its capital letters

parts.note: the first letter of each word, the two capitals of the title

explanation.surface: Who voices the big Looney Tunes stars in a Daffy Duck short?
explanation.walkthrough: Daffy Duck is a Looney Tunes star, so 'Daffy' hides as a name while signalling the shuffle. The capitals L and T sit inside the rearranged CARTOON.
explanation.definitionFit: A contralto is the lowest female singing voice, so it is a type of voice.

clue.text: Rod's sorry — as Spooner told panel

indicators.note: William Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words

parts.note: a rod is a cane; its opening sound is swapped with that of the next word
'sorry?' asks the same as 'what?'; its opening sound is swapped with that of the previous word

explanation.surface: Rod apologising, retold in the style of a tongue-tied clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of the two spoken words, C and W, and the rod and the question become a single wooden word.
explanation.definitionFit: Wainscot is wooden panelling lining the lower part of a room's walls, so a panel is a fair definition.

clue.text: Genghis Khan was one second before 12 noon and a little lunch

indicators.note: before means placed in front in the sequence

parts.note: a mo is a moment or second
N is the abbreviation for noon
12-across is GO-BETWEEN, read as an instruction to set GO between two pieces

indicators.note: a little of something is just a small bit, here its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: The great Khan grabbing a quick snack just before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: '12 noon' reads as midday, but 12 points to the answer of 12-across, GO-BETWEEN, so GO goes between N and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Genghis Khan founded the Mongol Empire and was a member of the Mongol people of central Asia.

clue.text: Scandinavian passport — perhaps for wife resulting in supplementary fare

indicators.note: one thing in place of another, as in swapping X for Y

parts.note: Swedish describes someone from Sweden
a passport is an example of ID
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A Swedish wife's passport leads to an extra charge on a ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: In SWEDISH, the W for wife is replaced by ID. 'Fare' suggests a travel ticket, but it means food.
explanation.definitionFit: A side dish is food served alongside the main course, an extra helping of fare in the food sense.

clue.text: Former PM keeping dry in a shelter

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside

parts.note: taken as written
TT is teetotal, abstaining from alcohol
the lee is the sheltered side away from the wind

explanation.surface: An ex-prime minister staying out of the rain in a bus shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: TT is the standard abbreviation for teetotal. Clement Attlee was the British Labour prime minister from 1945 to 1951.
explanation.definitionFit: Attlee led the British government after the Second World War, so he is a past prime minister.
